title: The staleness guard was blind between restarts; now the fingerprint survives them, proven on the wire
failures_first: The boundary fingerprint (#1126, #1131) was computed at seal time and kept only in a process-local dictionary. Measured: treeStateFingerprint on 0 of 58 tasks in the live store. This app relaunches constantly - after every release build and on every watchdog restart - so the staleness guard worked until the next restart and then went blind, with nothing saying so. The reading side was already wired (verdictTreeStates[task.id] ?? task.treeStateFingerprint); only the part that outlives the process was missing.

The day's Xcode update (Swift 6.0.3 -> 6.3.3) broke the shared QueenUILib interface three separate ways, and the build.sh probe knew only one signature: a neighbour's 6.0.3-stamped swiftmodule (version mismatch), XCTest moved out of the SDK so bare swiftc stopped finding it, and the module vanishing under a neighbour's wipe while SwiftPM still said 'Build complete'. Each was fatal until named.

Five full-gate attempts were collateral damage of active neighbours, not of the change: one e2e run failed 13 reaper checks because a neighbour's half-landed wasNeverStarted edit compiled mid-flight (the same suite passed before and after); make-dollars read a Makefile that existed for one minute; test-app was Terminated:15 by another run's pkill; the cassette lock queue stacked four agents deep; a warn-cache collision killed a nested make.

The cassettes step wedged for ten hours, and the mechanism is worth naming: the replay dispatches a REAL worker agent, that agent follows the project's own instructions and runs make check, and make check queues on the harness lock held by the very replay that spawned the worker. A self-deadlock by design collision. Killed at the 10-hour mark with the lock released.
did: QueenDelegationRegistry.recordTreeStateFingerprint(taskID:fingerprint:) writes the seal-time fingerprint onto the task record and persists; sealVerdictsWithBoundaryState calls it and logs queen.review.fingerprint_not_persisted when the task is gone. The in-memory dictionary remains for the live process; the record is what survives the restart.

Wire proof in the e2e suite, not a policy unit test: a hand-recorded /verify goes through the full command path, then the store FILE is decoded as a fresh reader (ISO8601 dates, no shared state) and both the fingerprint and the verdict are demanded on it. Passed in two clean full-suite runs: 971 of 971 checks each time.

build.sh: XCTest search path derived from xcrun --show-sdk-platform-path and added conditionally at all three import sites (module flags, the toolchain-compatibility probe, the vendored-interface probe - the last was reporting a healthy vendored module as broken). The probe's repair now engages on three signatures - foreign SDK, foreign compiler version, vanished module - and the repair rebuild falls back to the vendored halves on the neighbour-wipe signature, gated so a real compile error stays fatal.

Gate state, honestly: every step through test-app proven green in my runs (dev build, 0 warnings across 199 files, t27 gates, chain, vendor-step, test-app with the vendor probe fixed); the fingerprint work's own proof is the twice-green e2e.
